input:
A sample of a powder blend represents the batch only when the material in the sample has the same makeup as the material in the batch. A blend is not uniform by default. Its components differ in particle size and in density, and handling moves them apart: fine material settles through coarse material, and light material gathers where the blend has been poured or carried. Any one place in the batch can therefore differ from the batch as a whole.

Sampling answers that unevenness by spreading the taking across the batch. Increments are taken from points spread over the whole batch, from the top, the middle and the bottom of a container, and from across its width, and the increments together form one sample. No single increment is the sample. The sample carries the makeup of the batch because every part of the batch has contributed to it.

A single grab sample has no such defence. Taken from the surface, it reports the makeup of the surface, which settling and pouring have already separated from the bulk. A result from a grab sample can be precise and still wrong for the batch: the measurement is sound, and the material measured is not the material the result is applied to.
